title: Woven picot
subtitle: A free-standing woven loop that forms a detached leaf or petal shape
excerpt: Woven picot creates a free-standing triangular leaf or petal by weaving thread over a foundation pin or stitch. The woven triangle stands above the fabric surface and is anchored only at its base. Multiple woven picots together form a dimensional flower or leaf spray.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), detached stitches chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). Weldon's Practical Needlework, Vol. 4 (1888), picot leaf entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: A pin inserted at the tip of the woven picot shape. The foundation thread wraps around the pin to set the height of the woven triangle before weaving begins.

content.text: at the tip of the leaf to hold the foundation thread shape while weaving. Two threads extend from the base to the pin tip, forming a V. The weaving thread then fills the V from tip to base, going over and under the two foundation threads without entering the fabric. The pin is removed when weaving is complete.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton 2 strands or silk thread

items.label: Pin
items.value: A dressmaker's pin to hold the picot tip

items.label: Needle
items.value: Tapestry needle size 24 for weaving; embroidery needle for anchoring

content.text: Bring the thread up at the base of the leaf shape. Insert a pin at the tip position.
Loop the thread around the pin tip and bring the needle down at the other side of the base to form the V framework.
Bring the weaving thread up at the base. Weave over one foundation thread and under the other, alternating as you move toward the tip.
When the picot is fully woven, remove the pin and take the thread down at the base to secure it.

items.fix: Pack the weaving rows tightly from base to tip. The picot should hold its shape when the pin is removed.
items.symptom: The picot collapses when the pin is removed

items.fix: Both foundation threads must reach exactly to the pin tip. Check before starting to weave.
items.cause: The two foundation threads are not equal length.
items.symptom: The picot is not a neat triangle

content.text: Woven picot is a starting point for stumpwork and dimensional embroidery. The same pin-held weaving approach is used for raised leaves, petals, and insect wings in three-dimensional embroidery.
